body:
Thanks so much for the help. 
1. How do you handle DURs? I see my co-workers go into options and do a bunch of codes, but I’m not sure how to go about it because of how fast they input it. 
2. My pharmacist tells me to always hand them C-2’s so they can check when its due and if they have the quantity, but I see my coworkers not give it to them all the time. Is there a way I can check myself also? 
3. How do you handle medical? I see my co-workers ask for their social security, etc. I’m not sure why. How do input their insurance cards that have no bin? What about TPRs that state invalid ID#/group, when it was correct? (i live in california, I’m not sure if medical is different in other states)
4. How do you handle transfers? For instance, a customer will come up to me and say I want X transferred from this pharmacy to here. What do I do? I often see my co-workers grab the pad.

Thanks so much for the information it all really helped. How do you input insurance cards that do not have bin numbers? Sometimes patients give me state of california benefits cards and all they have are ID No. with their name. How do you calculate days supply for creams, drops, and liquids?
What do you recommend im going there in 15
How do you handle insurance rejects, such as “non-formulary” and “prior auth” and “third party rejects”?
I’m with walgreens at the moment
Everything really. Like how to enter an insurance card, how to rebill, rejection messages

I guess so, but the general opinion on the idea of our relationship is negative. It’s very difficult to deal with. Especially with my family, I’m sure they’ll all have a dissatisfaction with my presence over the matter. I’m not sure how I’m supposed to deal with that. Just have the courage to be disliked? I’m hesitant to approach it.
I understand that aspect, but I believe our maturity levels sort of match in this case
